title: Can a seven-distinction boundary shrink to six and conceal a legal three-parent join?
claim: Prove or realize a seven-to-six cut on the single-ternary branch of mixed serial parity, including proper shores and external witnesses. If reachable, separately test whether a full-table renaming changes an actual marked triple. If universally excluded, deduce the complete branch reader. Compare established radius statements with the published ring reader.
standard_statement: Determine whether a finite bipartite graph grown by constrained serial joins from a unique degree-three vertex can have a six-edge bond enclosing three or more ordinary vertices. Separate existence and minimum size from identifiability of a marked triple under permutations preserving all minimum common bond sizes.
prior_work: I proves the necessary first crossing. H excludes short cuts in specified sparse-exception sources. Candidate local delta.
completion_gate: Settle the existence of a genuine seven-to-six event on the single-ternary branch by a uniform exclusion or a literally verified reachable witness. Explicitly resolve its information consequences as far as the checked rival class supports, and state any remaining full-table question.
source_contribution: A history may certify the example; the anonymous reader receives only its present marked pair table.

validation.status: Independent within-task proof checks and six deterministic executable replays passed.

conclusion: A genuine seven-to-six boundary with a unique ternary seed first occurs at nine ordinary sites and 21 distinctions. At all finite sizes with only the first two unary additions making three outputs, distances through four determine every junction, allowed state and next join against arbitrary reachable rivals. This is sharp for a triple. The source may shrink again to five.
evidence_class: Size-independent counting and identification theorems with a finite fixed-point proof and literal witnesses.
target_disposition: The first crossing exists at the proved minimum. It and every source of the minimum-width class are all-rival identifiable. The fully unrestricted question continues on E.
unrestricted_obligation: Unrestricted full-table three-parent invariance remains open. A single-ternary opposing pair must use at least three three-output additions on each side. At exactly three, forcing the source equations suffices by the rank bound.
failure_conditions: A legal smaller shore or width, or an omitted nine-site equality shape.
A distance-four isometry changing a junction or join in the minimum-width source class, or a missing frontier transition.
A counterexample to the input-output arity lemma or the stated persistence hypotheses.
Failure to reproduce an indicated full-table or clipped comparison when the labels are transported.
